sovereign_country.strategic_role: 西欧核心消费市场、高客单价品牌合规与本土清关

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Motion Picture International Copyright Distribution and Licensing

applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: France–China Bilateral Investment Treaty (1984 amendment and exchange of notes)
France–United States Income Tax Convention (1967, as amended)
EU–Japan Economic Partnership Agreement (in force since 1 February 2019)
EU–Canada Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement / CETA (provisionally applied since 21 September 2017)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: French Monetary and Financial Code (Code monétaire et financier), Articles L.561-1 et seq. and R.561-1 et seq. (AML/CFT and PEP obligations); Code de commerce, Articles L.123-1 et seq. and R.123-166 (UBO declaration with the Registre du commerce et des sociétés), as transposing EU Directive 2015/849 (4AMLD) and Directive (EU) 2018/843 (5AMLD).

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of incorporation/good standing of any corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Domestic companies registry / chamber of commerce of the shareholder's jurisdiction

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarised copy of valid passport and proof of residential address for each UBO (beneficial owner at 25% or more) and the proposed manager (gérant)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the country of origin of each individual

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Irrevocable power of attorney granted to the French incorporation lawyer or representative to sign and file pre-incorporation formalities
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the country of origin

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs (subject to 25% threshold), directors, and authorized signatories against OFAC SDN List, the UN Security Council Consolidated List, the EU Consolidated List, TRACFIN domestic guidelines, and commercial adverse-media/PEP databases. Screening must occur at onboarding, immediately before incorporation, and at least annually thereafter. Any positive hit must be escalated and blocks any non-verified incorporation step.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Guichet unique of formalité de création (formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr by INPI); name search and RCS verification via Infogreffe (www.infogreffe.fr)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: All corporate names must be written in Latin script. A French name is not compulsorily required, but the proposed name must be distinct from prior existing names and not contrary to public policy or moral standards. If a foreign-language name is used, a French-language transliteration or evocation may be required to avoid confusion. Names reproducing a French word must respect French spelling and diacritical conventions.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: République / État / France when reserved to public institutions
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the INPI-RCS registry rejects a name on grounds of identity, confusion, or public order, the applicant receives a reasoned refusal notification. Within 15 calendar days from notification, the applicant may file a formal written appeal with the registry of the competent Tribunal de commerce or with the INPI overturning the refusal, and a copy of the appeal must be served on the opposing party if a third party raised an opposition. An alternative is judicial review before the Paris Tribunal de commerce or the Tribunal administratif (where applicable), each requiring legal representation. The same name may be resubmitted after modification only after a fresh availability search and within the 30-day reservation window.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: For an ISIC 5911 film-licensing SARL, a virtual office is commercially permissible if the registered office is domiciled under a professional domiciliation agreement (entreprise de domiciliation) authorized under Article L.123-11 of the Code de commerce. The domiciliation company must receive administrative documents and have a physical French address; however, tax and substance authorities may require actual management and accounting records to be accessible in France, particularly where the French entity claims French tax residence for film licensing income.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low to moderate. Quantified risk of unannounced on-site inspection: 5% in the first year for a standard non-regulated film licensing SARL; increases to 8% if UBO declarations are delayed or incomplete, and to 12% if the entity claims French tax benefits or intra-group licensing arrangements without commensurate local substance.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Company name availability search and trademark watch (Infogreffe + INPI screening)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for one name search and one-word trademark watch

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: RCS greffe registration fee for creating a Société à Responsabilité Limitée
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Greffe du tribunal de commerce (commercial registry clerk)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Fixed statutory tariff applicable to SARL registration under the Code des greffes des tribunaux de commerce

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Publication of the legal incorporation notice in a French mandatory legal announcements gazette (Journal d'annonces légales, JAL)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Designated legal gazette (Journal des Annonces Légales)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market tariff for one insertion in an approved JAL for a small SARL

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarization and apostille of foreign corporate and identity documents (bundle of up to three documents)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Notarial office of the country of origin / competent Hague Apostille authority
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory notarial tariff plus fixed government apostille fees per instrument

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Sworn translation (traduction assermentée) of apostilled foreign documents and draft French articles of association
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: French sworn translator (expert près de la cour d'appel)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark of approximately USD 30 per A4 page, estimated 6 to 7 pages

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered office domiciliation agreement - first-year contract and service fee
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark for a low-risk IP-licensing entity (approximately EUR 300 per year, excluding VAT)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Certificate of deposit of share capital (certificat de dépôt des fonds) issued by a French bank or Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Bank or financial institution in France
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Bank fee for issuance of a capital block deposit certificate for SARL formation

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: UBO declaration (déclaration de bénéficiaire effectif) preparation, filing, and administrative follow-up
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Guichet unique / Greffe via INPI intermediary
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Nominal processing fee in the official fee schedule for RCS attachments

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Pre-incorporation legal fees - drafting SARL statutes, AML/UBO clearance, PEP/sanctions screening, and first filing
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: French avocat / law firm registered at a Cour d'appel
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Negotiated fixed fee; prevailing market benchmark in France for a straightforward film-licensing SARL

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: French Commercial Code (Code de commerce), Articles L.223-1 to L.223-56 (SARL formation, management and operation), Decree No. 2023-362 on the Guichet Unique des Formalités des Entreprises, and R.123-1 et seq. on registration with the Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce of the registered-office jurisdiction, acting through the single electronic portal Guichet Unique des Formalités des Entreprises (INPI; sede.entreprises.gouv.fr)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Déclaration de constitution de société (CERFA form M0), filed fully electronically through the Guichet Unique, supplemented by the signed statutory articles and supporting attestations
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum share capital applies to an SARL (capital may be set at EUR 1); at least 20% of the cash subscription must be paid up at incorporation and the balance within 5 years (Article L.223-7, Code de commerce). Cash contributions must be deposited in a blocked account held by a licensed credit institution, a notary, or the Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations, and are released upon issuance of the Kbis certificate; in-kind contributions must be valued in the statuts and, when not waived unanimously, verified by a statutory auditor (commissaire aux apports).
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: The shareholders of [Company Name], acting as the constitutive general meeting of the Société à Responsabilité Limitée, hereby unanimously RESOLVE: (1) to approve the Articles of Association and to subscribe in full the share capital of EUR [•], each subscriber having deposited the cash contributions with [bank/notary/CDC] in accordance with Article L.223-7 of the French Commercial Code; (2) to adopt the registered office at [Address], France; (3) to appoint [Name] as first Manager (Gérant) for the whole corporate term, with full power to represent the company and to complete all incorporation formalities, including publication of the legal notice and filing before the Guichet Unique; (4) to ratify all preliminary acts accomplished on behalf of the company in formation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Pre-incorporation corporate name and entity screening
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: INPI — Institut National de la Propriété Industrielle (data.inpi.fr)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Run a conflict search on the INPI RCS database and the national trademark register for the proposed corporate name and its variants; verify that the name is distinctive, lawful, not misleading, and does not infringe an earlier mark. France does not issue a binding name-reservation certificate; the name is finally secured when the Greffe reproduces it on the Kbis extract.
required_dossiers: Proposed corporate name
Trademark and company-name screening report (internal record)
Identity particulars of the proposed shareholders and manager (for name consistency check)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a conflicting trademark or confusingly similar RCS name is identified, adopt an alternative distinctive name and amend the draft statuts before signature; retain the screening report as proof of due diligence in the corporate file.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and execution of the Articles of Association (Statuts)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Shareholders under private seal (sous seing privé) or a French notary (acte notarié) when real-estate contributions are made
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the statuts comprising the mandatory legal heads: SARL legal form, corporate name, object, registered office, duration (maximum 99 years), share capital in euros, number and nominal value of shares, cash and in-kind contributions, manager's powers, and dispute-resolution clause. Each shareholder must sign the single original or a true counterpart; a written domiciliation attestation from the lessor or an approved domiciliation agent is required. Electronic signature is permissible.
required_dossiers: Draft Articles of Association (statuts)
Passport or identity document of each shareholder
Proof of address of the manager (Gérant)
Domiciliation attestation signed by the lessor or domiciliation company
Statutory auditor's report on in-kind contributions (commissaire aux apports) unless unanimously waived
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a notary or the registry later identifies an unlawful or incomplete clause, the shareholders adopt a rectifying collective decision (résolution de régularisation) and re-execute the affected article by supplementary deed before filing the M0.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Blocked deposit of share capital and issuance of the blocking certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed French credit institution, French notary, or Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations (CDC)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary account in the name of the company 'en formation', transfer the cash contributions from each subscriber, and obtain from the depositary an attestation de blocage des fonds certifying the total paid-in amount and the blocked status of the funds. At least 20% of the cash subscription must be paid as of incorporation; the balance is due within five years. Funds remain unavailable until the Kbis certificate is issued.
required_dossiers: Shareholding and capital schedule
Cash contribution statements per subscriber
Blocking certificate (attestation de blocage des fonds)
Bank account opening form for the company in formation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank refuses account opening, invoke the statutory right to an account (droit au compte) with the Banque de France to compel designation of a paying institution; if the blocking certificate is inaccurate or incomplete, request a corrected certificate before submitting the M0.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publication of the incorporation notice in a legal announcement journal
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Journal d'Annonces Légales (JAL) accredited in the département of the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Insert the legal announcement (avis de constitution) containing the corporate name, legal form, share capital, registered office, corporate object, name of the manager, and reference to the deposit of funds; obtain the attestation de parution bearing the exact publication date and the journal's official announcement number.
required_dossiers: Statutory information sheet of the company
Identity of the first manager
Reference of the capital blocking deposit
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the JAL rejects or delays the insertion, correct the statutory data and republish in the same or another accredited journal; the publication certificate must precisely match the date required by the Guichet Unique for the registration file.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Electronic filing of the incorporation dossier (M0) on the Guichet Unique
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Guichet Unique des Formalités des Entreprises (INPI) — sede.entreprises.gouv.fr
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the digital M0 questionnaire and upload all annexes: executed statuts, capital blocking certificate, publication certificate, manager's sworn declaration of acceptance of office and absence of conviction, identity documents, registered-office domiciliation proof, and the beneficial-owners declaration (déclaration des bénéficiaires effectifs). The file is automatically routed to the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce, INSEE, URSSAF and the tax administration.
required_dossiers: Electronic M0/CERFA incorporation form
Signed Articles of Association
Capital blocking certificate (attestation de blocage des fonds)
Publication certificate of the legal announcement
Sworn declaration of the manager (déclaration de non-condamnation et d'acceptation des fonctions)
Domiciliation attestation of the registered office
Beneficial-owners declaration (RBE)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Guichet Unique or the Greffe issues an observation or incompleteness notice, cure within the prescribed régregularisation window (generally 30 days) by uploading the missing attachments; if the dossier is closed for non-compliance, file a new M0 with the corrected documents without loss of the underlying statutory acts.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: RCS registration and issuance of the Kbis extract
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce of the registered-office jurisdiction
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After substantive validation of the complete dossier, the Greffe registers the company in the Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés, attributes the definitive SIREN/SIRET identifiers and the APE code, and certifies legal existence by issuing the original extrait Kbis. The Kbis is the exclusive official evidence of incorporation and must be ordered from the Greffe either online or by post.
required_dossiers: Validated incorporation dossier transmitted by the Guichet Unique
Receipt of payment of the registration fee
Original blocking certificate for release instructions
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Kbis is not delivered within approximately ten business days from completeness, file a priority request with the Greffe and, if necessary, a petition before the President of the Tribunal de Commerce to order issuance; any clerical error in the Kbis entries is rectified through the Guichet Unique rectification procedure.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-registration tax, social and regulatory declarations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: URSSAF, Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP) and INSEE via the Guichet Unique notification channel
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Verify the transmission of the SIREN/SIRET to the competent tax office, confirm the default VAT registration status, and open the professional electronic account on the DGFiP 'espace professionnel'. If the company expects to hire employees, complete the employer registration with URSSAF before the first hire; verify the assigned APE code and check whether the legal thresholds impose the appointment of a statutory auditor (commissaire aux comptes).
required_dossiers: Kbis extract
Bank RIB/IBAN of the company account
Beneficial-owners declaration acknowledgement (RBE)
Professional tax account credentials
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Contest any erroneous APE code or VAT status before the Service des Impôts des Entreprises (SIE) attaching the Kbis and explanatory note; late employer registration with URSSAF is cured without penalty if completed within 30 days of the first recruitment.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: No industrial licensing board has competence for this activity; the business is confined to office-based film copyright distribution and licensing. The only sectoral administrative register is the CNC — Centre national du cinéma et de l'image animée, where a voluntary registration as a cinematographic distribution company may be effected to access French film-support mechanisms.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: None — no operating permit or manufacturing licence is required by law for international motion-picture copyright distribution and licensing. Voluntary CNC registration as a distribution company (Code du cinéma et de l'image animée) is recommended but does not condition lawful operation.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: DREAL — Direction régionale de l'environnement, de l'aménagement et du logement, acting under the préfet for any premises that might fall within the ICPE classification (Installations Classées pour la Protection de l'Environnement)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — full EIA registration does not apply. The activity triggers no installation threshold, discharge, or waste-producing operation listed in the Annex to Article R.122-2 of the French Environmental Code; no ICPE authorization or registration is required for standard administrative offices.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable for pure office operations. The company remains subject to the general municipal waste-sorting duty (Code de l'environnement, Articles R.541-12 et seq.) and to building energy-performance obligations; should a small audiovisual editing suite be installed, the general neighbourhood-noise emergence limit of 5 dB(A) applies, with no specific VOC or wastewater discharge standard triggered.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety and occupancy clearance: where office premises are open to the public, the ERP classification (Type L, école/établissement de loisir or Type R) must be declared to the Mairie and inspected by the commission de sécurité; for closed workplaces, compliance with the Labour Code Articles R.4222-1 to R.4227-14 (lighting, electrical installations, fire extinguishers, emergency exits, accessibility) suffices. Interior refit works exceeding 20 m² require a déclaration préalable de travaux filed at the Mairie; no structural load certification is required for non-assembly office use under the Construction and Housing Code.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP), Ministry of Economy and Finance, 10 rue du Centre, 93460 Noisy-le-Grand Cedex; national online portal: impots.gouv.fr (business portal: 'impots.gouv.fr / Mon espace professionnel'). VAT and corporate income tax (impôt sur les sociétés) are administered by the DGFiP; customs tariffs, EORI and export supervision by the Direction Générale des Douanes et Droits Indirects (DGDDI, douane.gouv.fr). Non-resident and foreign companies without a French establishment are handled centrally by the Service des Impôts des Entreprises Étrangères (SIEE) and by the Service des Impôts des Particuliers Non-Résidents (SIPNR) for personal income obligations.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France (Bank of France) as the national central bank, acting together with the Direction Générale du Trésor (French Treasury, part of the Ministère de l'Économie, des Finances et de la Souveraineté industrielle et numérique) on foreign-exchange and international-financial-relations matters; since France is in the euro area, exchange-rate policy is also governed by the European Central Bank (ECB) under the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union (TFEU, Articles 127-133) and the Eurosystem framework.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The euro (EUR) is fully convertible on both current and capital account. France has abolished all exchange-control restrictions since 1989-1990 (the last remnants of the 'réglementation des changes' were lifted in that period). The Code monétaire et financier (CMF, Articles L. 151-1 to L. 151-3 and R. 152-1 et seq.) guarantees freedom of financial relations with foreign countries in line with TFEU Articles 63-66 (free movement of capital and payments), subject only to limited safeguard derogations. In practice there is: (a) no prior authorisation for inbound capital or outbound profits/royalties; (b) no currency allocation, interest-equalisation or compulsory conversion regime; and (c) no regulatory distinction between current-account and capital-account transactions apart from statistical coding. The only hurdles for profit remittance from a French SARL to non-resident shareholders are corporate-law formalities (shareholders' resolution, verification of distributable reserves) and, depending on the shareholder's status, French withholding tax: a default 25% on dividends under Article 119 bis of the Code Général des Impôts (CGI) (12.8% for individuals; potentially reduced by tax treaty or exempt under the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive for qualifying EU corporate shareholders). None of these constitutes an exchange-control or convertibility barrier.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No export-proceeds surrender or mandatory conversion ratio exists in France. A French exporter may lawfully retain licensing income and royalties in foreign currency, convert them to EUR at free-market rates, or hold them on external accounts without any deadline or authorisation. The sole statutory obligation is the Banque de France balance-of-payments statistical declaration (reporting des changes): each cross-border payment reaching a resident account in an amount of EUR 12,500 or more is declared automatically by the receiving/issuing bank under the 3C reporting mechanism, and the company may be asked to confirm the underlying economic nature (goods, services, royalties, capital flows). Repeat small-value flows may be aggregated under a simplified quarterly declaration, but no individual conversion, repatriation, or surrender requirement applies.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account (EUR) with multi-currency overlay; documentary credit (LC issuance/confirmation) and escrow/segregated facilities available
Operational Account (EUR); dedicated Capital Escrow Account (compte séquestre) and commercial LC desk for large minimum-guarantee transactions
Operational Account (EUR, with EUR/USD dual-currency option)
Operational Account with USD-heavy coverage and trade-finance advisory for cross-border licensing flows

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Filing of annual certified financial statements (dépôt des comptes annuels) – balance sheet, income statement, and annexes
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Greffe du tribunal de commerce (commercial registry)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after fiscal year-end for approval; deposit within one month after approval, but no later than seven months after year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of EUR 150 (approx. USD 165) after 15 days; judicial order may impose daily fines; persistent non-filing triggers administrative strike-off (radiation) and loss of legal capacity.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax return (liasse fiscale n° 2065-SD) with annexes
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For fiscal year ending 31 December: filing due on the second business day after 1 May. For non-calendar fiscal year: within three months of year-end, with a possible one-month extension (total four months).
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing interest of 0.2% per month plus 5% penalty, increasing to 10% after one month; unauthorised non-filing yields 40% penalty and possible EUR 30,000 criminal fine.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual confirmation and update of the beneficial owner declaration (déclaration de bénéficiaires effectifs) – filed concurrently with annual accounts or within 30 days of any ownership change
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Greffe du tribunal de commerce (transmitted to the INPI central register)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: At the time of annual accounts filing; for any change in shareholding or control, within 30 days of the event
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: False statements subject to fine up to EUR 2,250 and possible prohibition; registry may refuse the annual accounts deposit; non-publicity may justify judicial prosecution.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual local business property contribution declaration and payment (cotisation foncière des entreprises – CFE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual declaration by 30 November; tax payable in one instalment mid-December (or in following months if amount under threshold); for companies newly subject, declaration due within six months of start.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Interest of 0.2% per month and a 10% penalty for late filing; administrative seizure of bank accounts in case of repeated default.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Statutory auditor (commissaire aux comptes) mandatory when a SARL exceeds two of the three following thresholds at fiscal year-end: total balance sheet > EUR 4,000,000; net turnover (excl. VAT) > EUR 8,000,000; average number of employees > 50. Subsidiaries or controlling entities may also trigger audit.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: French GAAP as codified in the Plan comptable général (PCG) and the French Commercial Code (Code de commerce). IFRS is permitted only for consolidated listed entities.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The beneficial owner register must be confirmed unless already updated within the prior year; annual confirmation is made by filing the declaration de bénéficiaires effectifs together with the statutory accounts deposit. Any share transfer must be registered in the securities transfer register (registre des mouvements de titres) within one month and reported to the registry if the manager is replaced or ownership changes effect control.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Directors and Managers (registre des décisions de gérance)
Minute Book (registre des procès-verbaux des assemblées générales)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 180 – 1,700 (typical annual domiciliation fee for a SARL at a commercial agent or legal office)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 8,000 – 35,000 (typical range for a statutory audit by a registered French firm for an independent film licensing company)

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Small and medium enterprise reduced rate of 15.00% pursuant to Article 219-I of the French General Tax Code (CGI) for taxable profits up to EUR 42,500 per fiscal year, available to companies with turnover below EUR 10,000,000 and share capital fully paid up and held at least 75% by individuals or qualifying small entities. Tax credit for R&D (Crédit d'Impôt Recherche - CIR) up to 30% of eligible expenditures. Tax credit for film and audiovisual production (Crédit d'Impôt International) applicable to qualifying independent film production and licensing entities. No general notional interest deduction; depreciation and amortization deductions available, including amortization of film intellectual property rights over the economic life of the rights.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 2065 (Déclaration de résultats) and accompanying schedules 2052 to 2059-N; forms 2031 and 2033-B for the reduced small and medium enterprise regime. Filed electronically via the Impôt Entreprise professional online portal (impots.gouv.fr / Gestion de l'IS)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Declarations must be filed within one month following the earlier of the 6-month corporate income tax filing deadline (déclaration de résultats) that is no later than the second business day following 1 May after the fiscal year close. For fiscal years ending 31 December, the filing deadline is the second business day after 1 May. Payment of corporate income tax is made through four quarterly instalments due on 15 March, 15 June, 15 September and 15 December, with the balance due on the filing deadline. If the entity is classified as a large company, the balance payment deadline may be extended to the second business day following 1 May, while the annual return (liassez fiscale) must be filed electronically by the same deadline.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Capital ownership allocation including shares held by individuals subject to French income tax, legal entities, and the share of capital held by non-resident shareholders with address outside France.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident shareholders directly or indirectly controlling more than 50% of the shares must be identified. Provide name, address, country of tax residence and percentage of ownership. For controlling non-resident entities, attach documentary evidence of tax residence, including a tax residence certificate where applicable.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Fiscal taxable result calculated before deduction of losses carried forward and tax credits; positive taxable income is subject to corporate income tax at the standard or reduced rate.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report worldwide income arising from the French permanent establishment or the French entity's activities. Independent film licensing revenues sourced from exploitation of rights in France must be included in full.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax loss carryforward from prior fiscal years deductible from current taxable income. Losses are indefinitely carried forward in France but the deductible portion for each fiscal year is capped at EUR 1,000,000 plus 50% of the taxable income exceeding that amount.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident entities operating through a French subsidiary may carry forward losses incurred in the French entity only if the continuity of business and the identity of shareholders are maintained. Substantive economic activity in France must be demonstrated for each loss year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax credits included in the corporate income tax balance, including CIR, film tax credits, and family tax credits (crédit d'impôt famille).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Tax credits are generally available only for French-source operating activities. Independent film licensing entities must substantiate eligible expenditures incurred in France and maintain contemporaneous records of production and licensing costs.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box QR / Réserve spéciale de participation
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Special employee profit-sharing reserve deduction calculated under the mandatory employee participation regime (intéressement et participation) for companies with more than 50 employees.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Applicable only if the French entity has French employees. For licensing-only vehicles without French payroll, leave blank.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net accounting income before tax from the statutory financial statements, reconciled to the tax result through the box 2058-A detailed reconciliation table.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The statutory financial statements must be prepared according to French GAAP (règlement ANC). Non-resident parent companies must attach consolidated or group financial statements only when requested by the tax administration.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty of 5% of the amount of tax due increased to 10% where the declaration is not filed within 30 days of a formal demand, plus 0.20% monthly interest on arrears (intérêt de retard) applied to unpaid tax from the statutory due date. Failure to file electronically results in a EUR 15,000 fixed penalty and possible 100% penalty on undeclared income where bad-faith or abusive tax evasion is established. Under Article 1728 CGI, the 10% increase applies if the return has not been submitted within 30 days of the mise en demeure. Additional 40% penalty for deliberate misconduct and 80% for dissimulation or abusive tax avoidance under Article 1729 CGI.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke treaty relief, the distributing French entity must obtain a Tax Residence Certificate (TRC) from the foreign parent company's tax authority, complete a French certificate of residence (form 5000 / attestation de résidence fiscale), and submit both to the French tax authorities before or at the time of the dividend distribution. Under an applicable DTA, the withholding tax rate is normally reduced to 0% or 15% depending on the treaty and shareholding thresholds; e.g., the France-Luxembourg DTA applies 0% if the parent company has held at least 10% of the distributing French company's capital for a minimum of 12 months and meets the anti-abuse conditions under Article 119 bis CGI and the DTA's limitation of benefits provisions. The French paying entity must file form 2561-bis with the Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP). The foreign parent must be the beneficial owner of the dividends. If the reduced treaty rate is applied at source, the parent must provide an annual certification of continued residence and shareholding; otherwise the excess withholding tax may be refunded through the ordinary refund procedure (réclamation contentieuse).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: statutory withholding tax of 33.33% on deemed French-source royalties under Articles 125-CGI and 182-B CGI where the beneficiary is non-resident; under most DTA treaties the rate is reduced to 0%, 5%, or 10%, subject to the beneficiary being the beneficial owner and the absence of a permanent establishment in France to which the IP is effectively connected. Interest: statutory withholding tax under Article 125-A CGI applies at 12.80% plus social levies (total 13.524%) on interest paid to non-resident beneficiaries; DTA rates are generally reduced to 0%, 10%, or 15% depending on the creditor and the absence of profit-participating character; the reduced treaty rate applies upon submission of form 5000 and TRC. For independent film licensing, royalties for the licensing of film distribution rights are treated as industrial and commercial income or copyright royalties; under the France-United States DTA, US licensors may obtain a 0% withholding tax on film and video royalties under the residual article if no French permanent establishment exists.

approved_arm_length_methodologies: CUP, Resale Price, Cost Plus, TNMM, Profit Split
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: The EU Anti-Tax Avoidance Directive (ATAD) and French Economic Substance jurisprudence require that the French licensing entity demonstrates real economic substance. Although France does not maintain formal Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) akin to the UAE or Cayman, the French General Tax Code (Article 155-A, 1655-A, and 209-B) and the OECD Base Erosion and Profit Shifting (BEPS) framework require the French SARL to show substantive activity, including: (i) local management and decision-making in France; (ii) employees with technical competence in film licensing, contract negotiation, and copyright supervision; (iii) premises and operational equipment commensurate with the volume of licensing contracts; (iv) actual control over film rights including registration in France, and (v) assumption of material economic risk. A French-resident licensing SARL that merely channels film royalties to a foreign parent without staff or substance is vulnerable to recharacterization as an abuse of law under L-64 Livre des procédures fiscales, or to taxation of the profits in the hands of the non-resident beneficiary under Article 155-A when the entity is interposed and controlled by non-residents unless the SARL demonstrates a legitimate commercial purpose and actual economic substance. The French tax administration also applies OECD BEPS Action 3 controlled foreign company (CFC) rules and the principal purpose test under the EU ATAD. A written substance file with employment contracts, board minutes, invoices, licensing agreements, and the bank account records must be contemporaneously maintained.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Intentional omission or undervaluation of film licensing revenues derived from French distribution agreements; concealment of royalty receipts in offshore accounts; deliberate use of fictitious intermediary companies or non-existent licenses to reduce taxable income; submission of false tax returns under Article 1741 CGI.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Imprisonment of up to 5 years and a fine of EUR 500,000, which may be increased to 50% of the evaded tax amount and up to EUR 3,000,000 in aggravated cases under Article 1741-1 CGI. Additional 40% penalty for deliberate misconduct and 80% penalty for abusive tax avoidance under Article 1729 CGI, plus late payment surcharges and daily interest.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and officers may be criminally prosecuted personally; the corporate veil may be pierced. They may be ordered to pay the evaded tax and penalties jointly and severally with the company. The court may impose travel bans, prohibitions on managing a commercial enterprise (Article L-653-8 Code de commerce), and imprisonment of 5 years. Directors who deplete corporate assets to frustrate tax recovery may be subject to bankruptcy sanction of bankruptcy (faillite personnelle) with a ban of up to 15 years from directing and managing a business.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Abuse of Law (Abus de droit)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Establishing a French SARL as an intermediary for film licensing without genuine economic activities, without local employees, without local decision-making, or with the sole purpose of obtaining French treaty benefits, reduced withholding rates, or to avoid taxation in the beneficiary jurisdiction. Interposition of the entity between the foreign licensor and French film distributors without substantive commercial justification.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The tax administration may set aside the artificial arrangement and tax the profit in the hands of the true beneficiary; a penalty of 80% of the reassessed tax may be imposed under Article 1729-b CGI. In addition, a specific administrative abuse procedure (Article L-64 A LPF) allows sanctions against professional advisors who design abusive tax arrangements, with fines up to EUR 10,000 or 50% of the professional fees. The company is subject to recharacterization with all tax benefits revoked.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly participate in setting up or maintaining an artificial shell entity are jointly liable for the resulting tax liability under Article L-266 LPF, including penalties and interests. Failure to file annual returns may trigger administrative dissolution proceedings; in cases of fraudulent dissimulation, directors face up to 5 years imprisonment and personal fines of EUR 75,000 under Article 1741 CGI. In insolvency proceedings, a manager may incur the entire unpaid corporate debts where the management conduct has contributed to the insufficiency of assets under Article L-651-2 Code de commerce.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Charging non-arm's-length royalty rates for film licensing between the French SARL and foreign affiliated entities, including obtaining excessively large markups on sublicensed rights, paying inflated royalties to a related overseas parent, or allocating profits to low-tax jurisdictions without cost contribution arrangements in accordance with the OECD TP Guidelines and Article 57 CGI.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Reassessment of profits to the arm's-length amount under Article 57 CGI. Unjustified transfer pricing adjustments trigger a 40% good-faith penalty or 80% penalty for abuses of rights. Documents may be required under Article L-13 B LPF; failure to submit TP documentation within 30 days of a formal request results in a fine of EUR 15,000, plus the application of a 5% penalty on the reassessed amount if the documentation obligation is not fulfilled, capped at EUR 10,000 per transaction.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who prepare or approve fraudulent transfer pricing documentation may be liable for the additional assessments due to their gross negligence. Criminal exposure arises where documentation is knowingly falsified: penal sanctions apply under Article 1741 CGI and corporate directors could face jail terms of 5 years and fines of EUR 500,000. In cross-border group restructuring, directors may also face personal liability for illegal distributions if the French SARL is unable to pay its creditors.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Non-Filing and Failure to Cooperate with Tax Audit
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to file the annual corporate tax returns, failure to submit financial statements to the Commercial Court registry, refusal to respond to a tax audit demand (droit de communication), or obstruction of the tax inspector during an audit under Article L-16-0 A LPF.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fine of EUR 10,000 for failure to file financial statements at the Commercial Registry; a 5% or 10% late-filing penalty on corporate income tax as described under Article 1728 CGI; 100% penalty on undeclared tax where bad faith is established. For unregistered commercial activities, tax evasion sanctions under Article 1741 CGI apply. Simple non-filing of the annual return for more than 60 days after the formal demand triggers an automatic 10% increase.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The legal representative may be subject to a tax audit penalty of up to EUR 1,000 personally under Article 1732 CGI when the representative fails to answer tax inquiries. Where the failure to file causes losses for the tax authority, the director is jointly and severally liable for taxes, penalties, and interest; imprisonment is possible in aggravated cases involving concealment. In respect of the registration duty on bad-faith non-filing, the person may be banned from managing a commercial company for up to 5 years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Receiving licensing fees in cash above EUR 1,000 or through unlicensed payment channels; conducting transactions with sanctioned film distributors or acting for a person subject to an EU asset freeze without the required authorization; deliberate failure to declare suspicious transactions to Tracfin where the entity is considered a déclarant; intentional use of SWIFT wire or letter-of-credit arrangements to disguise the origin or destination of film licensing payments.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Violations of the French Monetary and Financial Code (Article L-561-42) carry fines of up to EUR 750,000 for entities and EUR 375,000 for individuals; criminal sanctions for money laundering under Article 324-1 of the French Criminal Code may result in imprisonment of up to 10 years and a fine of EUR 750,000, increased to EUR 5,000,000 where the laundering has an organized-crime dimension. Violation of EU restrictive measures triggers individual criminal liability and asset freeze enforcement.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and officers face personal criminal prosecution for AML breaches; corporate veil does not shield fraudulent transfers. Directors may be imprisoned up to 10 years and subjected to confiscation of assets. They are also exposed to civil liability under Article L-651-2 Code de commerce if they have misused corporate assets in facilitating laundering schemes, with travel bans and professional disqualification up to 15 years.
